issues.body:
The workflow invokes `python3 scripts/backfill-targets.py` with no `--requested` flag and binds the operator's choice through `env: REQUESTED: ${{ inputs.target_repo }}`. So the ONLY production path into the narrowing/refusal logic is main()'s line 114:

    requested = os.environ.get("REQUESTED", "") if args.requested is None else args.requested

Nothing exercises that line with a non-empty env value:

- backfill-targets.py `_self_test` calls `main(["--policy", ..., "--requested", ...])` for both the success and unknown-target rows, so `args.requested is None` is never False... rather, never True. The env branch is dead in this suite.
- backfill-provenance.py `_resolve_step_result` (the only harness that actually runs `main()`) hard-pins `env = {..., "REQUESTED": ""}` at line 1913, and its comment openly defers the requested-target paths to `_resolve_targets`.
- backfill-provenance.py `_resolve_targets` no longer runs `main()` at all (see below), so it no longer covers them either.

Mutant that survives everything: change line 114 to `requested = args.requested or ""`. Then a manual `workflow_dispatch` for `zzz-fixture/gamma` (disabled) or an unknown repo no longer refuses — it silently widens to the full enabled sweep. Both scripts' `--self-test` stay 100% green, `_resolve_step_result` stays green (it pins REQUESTED=""), and the seam report stays green (it only asserts the YAML text `${{ inputs.target_repo }}`, i.e. the producer, never the consumer).

That is precisely the property backfill-provenance.py:1944-1949 says it is protecting ("must never admit a non-policy target (the sol r1 arbitrary-repo class), and must never silently widen to the whole sweep instead") — and before this diff it WAS protected, because `exec(_resolver_src, {"__name__": "__main__"})` ran the heredoc's own `os.environ.get("REQUESTED")` read.
issues.fix_hint:
Add rows to `_self_test` in scripts/backfill-targets.py that drive main() through the ENV seam with `--requested` absent, restoring/saving os.environ["REQUESTED"] around them. Both directions, since the mutant collapses them into one:

    saved = os.environ.get("REQUESTED")
    try:
        os.environ["REQUESTED"] = "fixture/one"
        out = io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out):
            status = main(["--policy", str(policy_path)])
        check("bare CLI narrows using the REQUESTED env binding the workflow sets",
              (status, out.getvalue().strip()), (0, 'repos=["fixture/one"]'))
        os.environ["REQUESTED"] = "fixture/unknown"
        err = io.StringIO()
        with contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):
            status = main(["--policy", str(policy_path)])
        check("an unknown REQUESTED refuses via env too — never a silent full sweep",
              (status, "not an ENABLED policy row" in err.getvalue()), (1, True))
    finally:
        os.environ.pop("REQUESTED", None)
        if saved is not None:
            os.environ["REQUESTED"] = saved

The second row is the load-bearing one: use a policy fixture with a DIFFERENT enabled row present, so the mutant's widened sweep is a distinguishable non-refusal rather than an incidentally-empty result. Alternatively (or additionally) parameterise `_resolve_step_result` in backfill-provenance.py to take the REQUESTED value instead of hard-coding "", and add a shell-seam refusal row for a disabled target.
issues.title: No test executes main()'s REQUESTED env fallback with a non-empty value — a silent-widening mutant survives both self-tests

issues.body:
At lines 1854-1859 the harness exec's the helper under `__name__ = "backfill_targets"` (so `main()` and the `if __name__ == "__main__"` block never run), calls `resolve_file` directly, and then the TEST itself does `print("repos=" + json.dumps(result))` inside the capture buffer.

Consequence: the `("repos", [...])` tuple compared at lines 1938-1943 has an output-name half and a JSON-encoding half that are produced by the harness, not by the code under test. The partition/`json.loads` round-trip at lines 1869-1876 is now decoding a string this same function just encoded — it cannot fail. So the check name "the resolver emits EVERY enabled policy row (sorted) as JSON under the name `repos`" over-claims: only the list value is shipped-code-derived. A mutant printing `repo=` or a bare JSON array is invisible here.

This is not fully vacuous — `_resolve_step_result(_POLICY)` at line 1958 does run the real `main()` through bash and exact-matches `repos=["zzz-fixture/alpha", "zzz-fixture/beta"]` in $GITHUB_OUTPUT, which does kill that mutant for the REQUESTED="" case. But the row's stated claim and what it proves have drifted apart, which is the kind of drift this file's own comments treat as a defect.

Secondary nit in the same block: `exec` and the `resolve_file` call now sit OUTSIDE `redirect_stdout(buffer)`, so stray output from the helper escapes the `UNPARSED` guard rather than reding it (still caught downstream at the shell seam, since a stray print would flow through `tee` into $GITHUB_OUTPUT).
issues.fix_hint: Either (a) call the shipped entry point so the assertion means what its name says — e.g. `namespace["main"](["--policy", "policy/repos.toml"])` inside `redirect_stdout(buffer)`, letting the helper emit its own `repos=`/JSON (this also closes the major issue above, since main() would then read REQUESTED from the env the harness sets at lines 1848-1851); or (b) keep the direct `resolve_file` call but rename the affected checks to state what they actually prove ("the resolver DERIVES every enabled policy row (sorted) from policy") and rely on `_resolve_step_result` for the output-name claim. Option (a) is strictly better here. Also move `exec`/`resolve_file` inside the `redirect_stdout` block so unexpected stdout still reds the `UNPARSED` guard.
issues.title: `_resolve_targets` now asserts the harness's own print, so the `repos=`/JSON half of its check names is no longer proven by shipped code

issues.body: `backfill_targets_resolver_source` no longer extracts a heredoc, but references survive: the failure reason at line 1327 reads "the resolver's heredoc does not compile" (it is now the helper file that failed to compile, and the operator would go looking in the workflow), and the section comment at line 1828 still says "by executing the shipped heredoc". `_resolve_step_result`'s docstring at line 1887 likewise says "`_resolve_targets` above executes only the heredoc's PYTHON". The compile error message is the one that matters — it names the wrong file to a reader debugging a red suite. The `<targets.resolve>` compile filename at line 1325 is similarly now misleading.
issues.fix_hint: s/heredoc/helper/ in the reason string at line 1327, the comment at line 1828, and the docstring at line 1887; change the `compile()` filename at line 1325 from `"<targets.resolve>"` to `"scripts/backfill-targets.py"` so a SyntaxError points at the real file.
issues.title: Stale "heredoc" wording left behind after the heredoc was removed

verdict.summary:
The refactor itself is sound and well-motivated: the resolver heredoc becomes a checked-in, independently self-tested helper (scripts/backfill-targets.py), the thin sparse-checkout is widened to carry it and that widening is pinned by a new exact-match seam row, the shell command sequence assertion is updated to the exact three-line sequence, and the shell execution seam (_resolve_step_result) still runs the whole shipped `run` block through bash and asserts both the refusal exit status and the literal `repos=[...]` written to $GITHUB_OUTPUT. `_split_heredoc` is fully removed with no dangling callers; `textwrap` is still used elsewhere. Fail-closed behaviour in the helper is stronger than the heredoc it replaces (`enabled is True` rather than truthiness, an explicit `repos` table check, a typed TargetResolutionError). Permissions, SHA pinning, and the `env:`-bound (never shell-interpolated) REQUESTED binding are all preserved. No token/PII exposure.

Blocking concern is test validity, and it is a REGRESSION this diff introduces. Previously `_resolve_targets` ran `exec(_resolver_src, {"__name__": "__main__"})`, so the heredoc's top-level `requested = os.environ.get("REQUESTED")` read was exercised by the four requested-target rows. The new harness exec's the helper under a non-main `__name__` and calls `resolve_file(path, os.environ.get("REQUESTED", ""))` itself, so those rows now bypass `main()` entirely. Nothing anywhere — not backfill-provenance.py's harness (which pins REQUESTED="" at the shell seam) and not backfill-targets.py's own self-test (which always passes `--requested` explicitly) — executes `main()`'s env fallback with a non-empty value. Mutating that one line to ignore REQUESTED turns a manual dispatch of an unknown or DISABLED target from a loud refusal into a silent full sweep — the exact sol-r1 arbitrary-repo widening that check at backfill-provenance.py:1946 claims to kill — with every self-test in both scripts still green. One added row fixes it.
